knowledge:
- key_parameters: path_to_fcs=Path to the folder containing input FCS files ;; path_to_output=Path to the folder where output files (FCS, PDFs) will be saved ;; backbone_selection_file=CSV file specifying which channels are backbone, exploratory, or discard ;; annotation=Named vector of Infinity antibody targets per FCS file (names are FCS file names) ;; isotype=Named vector of Infinity antibody isotypes per FCS file (names are FCS file names) ;; input_events_downsampling=Number of events to downsample per input file for model training (e.g., 1000, 20000, 50000) ;; prediction_events_downsampling=Number of events to downsample for prediction/output (e.g., 500, 10000) ;; cores=Number of cores for parallel computing ;; regression_functions=List of fitter functions (e.g., fitter_xgboost, fitter_svm, fitter_glmnet, fitter_linear, fitter_nn) to train ;; extra_args_regression_params=List of lists containing hyperparameters matched by order to regression_functions
- alternatives: The package supports multiple regression backends via fitter functions: fitter_xgboost (default, XGBoost), fitter_nn (Tensorflow/Keras neural networks), fitter_svm (e1071 SVM), fitter_glmnet (L1-penalized polynomial models), and fitter_linear (linear/polynomial models).
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing massively parallel cytometry experiments where a sample is aliquoted into multiple subsamples, each stained with a shared "Backbone" panel and a unique "Infinity" exploratory antibody.
- pitfalls: High memory usage can occur if input_events_downsampling and prediction_events_downsampling are set too high initially; start with low values and ramp up. There is a known serialization issue with neural networks and socketing in R >= 4.0.1; if using fitter_nn, cores must be set to 1L.

workflows.name: basic_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the standard Infinity Flow pipeline using the default XGBoost regression model to predict exploratory marker expression.
input: steady_state_lung_annotation (data frame of targets and isotypes annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and example data ;; 2. Define paths for input, output, and intermediary results ;; 3. Set up target and isotype annotation vectors ;; 4. Run the pipeline using infinity_flow()
workflows.code:
library(infinityFlow)
data(steady_state_lung)
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "infinity_flow_example")
print(dir)
input_dir <- file.path(dir, "fcs")
write.flowSet(steady_state_lung, outdir = input_dir) ## Omit this if you already have FCS files
list.files(input_dir)
data(steady_state_lung_annotation)
print(steady_state_lung_annotation)
# backbone_specification <- select_backbone_and_exploratory_markers(list.files(input_dir, pattern = ".fcs", full.names = TRUE))
data(steady_state_lung_backbone_specification)
print(head(steady_state_lung_backbone_specification))
write.csv(steady_state_lung_backbone_specification, file = file.path(dir, "backbone_selection_file.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
list.files(dir)
path_to_fcs <- file.path(dir, "fcs")
head(list.files(path_to_fcs, pattern = ".fcs"))
path_to_output <- file.path(dir, "output")
list.files(dir)
backbone_selection_file <- file.path(dir, "backbone_selection_file.csv")
head(read.csv(backbone_selection_file))
targets <- steady_state_lung_annotation$Infinity_target
names(targets) <- rownames(steady_state_lung_annotation)
isotypes <- steady_state_lung_annotation$Infinity_isotype
names(isotypes) <- rownames(steady_state_lung_annotation)
head(targets)
head(isotypes)
input_events_downsampling <- 1000
prediction_events_downsampling <- 500
cores = 1L
path_to_intermediary_results <- file.path(dir, "tmp")
imputed_data <- infinity_flow(
	path_to_fcs = path_to_fcs,
	path_to_output = path_to_output,
	path_to_intermediary_results = path_to_intermediary_results,
	backbone_selection_file = backbone_selection_file,
	annotation = targets,
	isotype = isotypes,
	input_events_downsampling = input_events_downsampling,
	prediction_events_downsampling = prediction_events_downsampling,
	verbose = TRUE,
	cores = cores
)

workflows.name: custom_regression_pipeline
workflows.intent: Run the Infinity Flow pipeline using custom regression models (e.g., SVM, LASSO, Linear Model) and custom hyperparameters.
input: steady_state_lung_annotation (data frame of targets and isotypes annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Load package and prepare data paths and annotations ;; 2. Define custom regression functions list ;; 3. Define corresponding hyperparameter list ;; 4. Run the pipeline using infinity_flow() with custom regression arguments
workflows.code:
library(infinityFlow)

data(steady_state_lung)
data(steady_state_lung_annotation)
data(steady_state_lung_backbone_specification)

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "infinity_flow_example")
input_dir <- file.path(dir, "fcs")
write.flowSet(steady_state_lung, outdir = input_dir)

write.csv(steady_state_lung_backbone_specification, file = file.path(dir, "backbone_selection_file.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

path_to_fcs <- file.path(dir, "fcs")
path_to_output <- file.path(dir, "output")
path_to_intermediary_results <- file.path(dir, "tmp")
backbone_selection_file <- file.path(dir, "backbone_selection_file.csv")

targets <- steady_state_lung_annotation$Infinity_target
names(targets) <- rownames(steady_state_lung_annotation)
isotypes <- steady_state_lung_annotation$Infinity_isotype
names(isotypes) <- rownames(steady_state_lung_annotation)

input_events_downsampling <- 1000
prediction_events_downsampling <- 500
cores = 1L
regression_functions <- list(
    XGBoost = fitter_xgboost, # XGBoost
    SVM = fitter_svm, # SVM
    LASSO2 = fitter_glmnet, # L1-penalized 2nd degree polynomial model
    LM = fitter_linear # Linear model
)
backbone_size <- table(read.csv(backbone_selection_file)[,"type"])["backbone"]
extra_args_regression_params <- list(
     ## Passed to the first element of `regression_functions`, e.g. XGBoost. See ?xgboost for which parameters can be passed through this list
    list(nrounds = 500, eta = 0.05),
    # Passed to the third element, SVMs. See help(svm, "e1071") for possible arguments
    list(type = "nu-regression", cost = 8, nu=0.5, kernel="radial"),
    # Passed to the fourth element, fitter_glmnet. This should contain a mandatory argument `degree` which specifies the degree of the polynomial model (1 for linear, 2 for quadratic etc...). Here we use degree = 2 corresponding to our LASSO2 model Other arguments are passed to getS3method("cv.glmnet", "formula"),
    list(alpha = 1, nfolds=10, degree = 2),
    # Passed to the fourth element, fitter_linear. This only accepts a degree argument specifying the degree of the polynomial model. Here we use degree = 1 corresponding to a linear model.
    list(degree = 1)
)
if(length(regression_functions) != length(extra_args_regression_params)){
    stop("Number of models and number of lists of hyperparameters mismatch")
}
imputed_data <- infinity_flow(
	regression_functions = regression_functions,
	extra_args_regression_params = extra_args_regression_params,
	path_to_fcs = path_to_fcs,
	path_to_output = path_to_output,
	path_to_intermediary_results = path_to_intermediary_results,
	backbone_selection_file = backbone_selection_file,
	annotation = targets,
	isotype = isotypes,
	input_events_downsampling = input_events_downsampling,
	prediction_events_downsampling = prediction_events_downsampling,
	verbose = TRUE,
	cores = cores
)
